# AI review: what each label means

AI-reviewed means a named, versioned check was run on this claim and passed: either a rule written as code, or a specialist AI reviewer that saw only the evidence packet. It never means a person has checked it. Human reviews are listed separately, each under the reviewer’s name.

There are two kinds, never blurred. **Checked by rule**: deterministic code, recorded with the procedure id, version and code hash; no model. **AI specialist review**: a model working as a specialist reviewer from a saved system prompt, cut off from how the claim was produced, recorded with the model id, the prompt hash, the packet hash and UTC start and finish times. The public page is `/method`; each heading below is its anchor.

Where a procedure has no measured accuracy, this page says so.

## Who a name in a chain refers to {#identity}

Every candidate identity for a name is kept with its basis. Where sources disagree, all are shown and none is preferred.

### Source index confirmed by the Arabic text {#identity-source-index-confirmed-by-text}

`identity-source-index-confirmed-by-text` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** The six-books source ships its own narrator index for each chain. The identity stands when the source names this person at this position, the name written in the Arabic agrees with that person’s recorded name position by position (or every source id aligns across the branches), and no other candidate names someone else. A kunya-only match never counts against it.

**Evidence.** The report’s Arabic text and its extracted chain, bound by the text’s SHA-256; The source’s narrator index for the report (K6 chain_indx), read from the original file; The narrator lexicon’s recorded names for each indexed person.

**Measured.** Where this rule and hadith-kg (an independent compilation) both identify a name and both are confirmed by the text, they pair the same way for 19,855 of 20,972 mentions (94.7 %). A separate reading found about one in twenty wrong where two people share a name. Sample: Agreement: 20,972 co-claimed Sunni mentions, measured by code (a floor, not a precision). The one-in-twenty reading: one reader; sample size not recorded in the repository. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/source-identity/README.md; src/db/AGENTS.md §Standing identity`.

**Known failure modes.** Shared opening tokens let a wrong index pass (قيس بن أبي غرزة confirmed as قيس بن أبي حازم through قيس بن أبي); Bare isms shared by several men (سفيان, خالد) when the source commits to one of them; Duplicate lexicon rows for one man look like two people.

**Reader sees.** “AI-reviewed (checked by rule): the source’s index and the text agree”

**Excluded.** Placeholder lexicon rows (single word, kunya only, no Arabic name, unidentified shaykh) are never a target.

**Credited.** `K6I` K6 source narrator index (Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-dataset”, chain_indx); `MSD` Muslim Scholars Database, Arees Institute (via Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-narrators”); `SUN` sunnah.com (via Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-dataset”).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/reconciled/build_k6_source_index_sidecar.py`, `datasets/hadith-data/pg_export/export_postgres.py`.

### Source index without full confirmation {#identity-source-index}

`identity-source-index` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** The source’s index names a person at a position the Arabic corroborates, but the report as a whole does not agree position by position. The claim is shown as the source’s, not as AI-reviewed.

**Evidence.** The source’s narrator index; The aligned positions of the Arabic chain.

**Measured.** Across all co-claimed Sunni mentions, the source index and hadith-kg pair the same way for 90,295 of 96,331 (93.7 %). Sample: 96,331 mentions, measured by code; agreement between two sources, not a precision. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/source-identity/README.md`.

**Known failure modes.** A position shift in a report where the source counts names differently from the text.

**Reader sees.** “Source index (the source’s claim; not AI-reviewed)”

**Credited.** `K6I` K6 source narrator index (Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-dataset”, chain_indx).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/pg_export/export_postgres.py`.

### Name match against the narrator lexicon {#identity-name-match}

`identity-name-match` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** In Sunni reports only, the name as written matches exactly one lexicon entry, letter for letter or after five fixed spelling folds. A name shared by several entries never matches. The match is a candidate, never AI-reviewed.

**Evidence.** The name as written; The lexicon’s names after the same folds.

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. No precision has been measured for name matches. They are shown only as candidates for that reason.

**Known failure modes.** Two people with one recorded name where the lexicon holds only one of them.

**Reader sees.** “Matched by name (a candidate; not AI-reviewed)”

**Excluded.** Imami, Ibadi and Zaydi reports get no name candidate (owner decision: sanads stay within their tradition).

**Credited.** `MSD` Muslim Scholars Database, Arees Institute (via Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-narrators”).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/regen_unified_csvs.py`.

### Kunya-only match (a label) {#identity-kunya-only}

`identity-kunya-only` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** The only match is on a kunya. It is shown as a labelled note, never contests another identity, and is left out of every analysis.

**Evidence.** The name as written; Lexicon entries that are a kunya alone.

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. Not measured; by owner decision it is a label, not an identification.

**Known failure modes.** Many narrators share one kunya.

**Reader sees.** “Matched by kunya only (a label)”

**Credited.** `MSD` Muslim Scholars Database, Arees Institute (via Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-narrators”).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/regen_unified_csvs.py`.

### The Imams’ conventional kunyas in Imami chains {#identity-imam-kunya-convention}

`identity-imam-kunya-convention` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · Adopted, not yet loaded

**Rule.** In an Imami chain, a name that is exactly one of the listed kunyas, optionally with a listed qualifier, followed by the honorific marker, names that Imam. A kunya several Imams share, with no qualifier, gives a labelled candidate for each, never AI-reviewed. Any other words after the kunya mean it is not an Imam.

**Evidence.** The name as written with its marker; The convention table (reviewable data, not a scholarly claim).

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. Not yet measured. The specialist pilot includes a sample of these mentions.

**Known failure modes.** A non-Imam narrator with the same kunya and a marker added by a copyist.

**Reader sees.** “AI-reviewed (checked by rule): the Imams’ conventional kunya”

**Excluded.** Sunni, Ibadi and Zaydi chains.

**Credited.** `THQ` Thaqalayn (Stichting Thaqalayn); `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/pg_export/imam_kunya.py`, `datasets/hadith-data/pg_export/imam_kunya_conventions.json`.

### Relation words read through the work’s opening isnad (Musnad Zayd) {#identity-opening-isnad}

`identity-opening-isnad` version `2026.11.22` · Checked by rule · Adopted, not yet loaded

**Rule.** In Musnad Zayd, a chain of exactly the shape «زيد بن علي، أبيه، جده، علي» (or its first two or three links) names the persons the work’s own first report names: Zayd b. ʿAli, ʿAli b. al-Husayn, al-Husayn b. ʿAli, ʿAli b. Abi Talib. Any other shape gets nothing.

**Evidence.** The work’s report No. 1 («حدثني زيد بن علي عن ابيه علي بن الحسين عن جده الحسين بن علي ...»); The chain shape as written.

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. Not yet measured by a reviewer; 617 chains take the rule.

**Known failure modes.** A report whose «أبيه» refers to someone other than Zayd’s father (the shape check excludes any other first name).

**Reader sees.** “AI-reviewed (checked by rule): the work’s opening isnad names him”

**Excluded.** Every other work and every other chain shape.

**Credited.** `OITI` OpenITI: a Machine-Readable Corpus of Islamicate Texts; `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/pg_export/chain_builder.py`, `datasets/hadith-data/pg_export/opening_isnad_rules.json`.

**Evidence.** Both sources’ claims at the position; The lexicon link between their two narrator records.

`identity-external-source-claims` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** A dataset’s narrator id is that dataset’s claim, carried onto our chain only at positions the Arabic corroborates. Riwayat’s automatic linking never counts toward AI-reviewed.

### Which chains feed teacher and student lists {#chain-structure-gate}

`chain-structure-gate` version `2026.11.22` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** Each stored chain is tested for shapes that the re-checks found wrong: a name stored twice in a row, two names in one position, words that are not a name, text that names more than the chain holds, more «ح» or «جميعا» than stored routes, three or more routes in one six-books report, and the 15 small Imami works whose chains were read wrong most often. A chain that trips any test is still shown as stored, marked unchecked with its reasons, and forms no teacher–student pair. Chains of Kitab al-Duafa, Risalat al-Huquq and chapter headings are not stored as chains.

**Evidence.** The chain as stored; The report’s Arabic (the source’s own chain field for Pure Canon); The other routes of the report.

**Measured.** Re-check of 2026-11-22 (round 3), random sample, strict defects before the gate → among chains left checked: Sunni 18.0% → 2.6% (76 of 100 chains kept; six-books text works 25.4% → 4.3%, 47 of 67); Imami 17.0% → 3.2% (63 of 100); al-Rabiʿ 16.1% → 7.7% (26 of 31: not shown below 5%); Musnad Zayd 2.5% → 0% (39 of 40); Sahifat al-Rida 0% → 0% (40 of 40). Over all 980 read units: 12.1% → 2.2%. Share of stored chains checked (projection 2026.11.22.9): Sunni 73.2% (six-books text works 68.0%, Pure Canon 80.9%), Imami 61.0% (al-Kafi 91.3%), al-Rabiʿ 95.0%, Musnad Zayd 99.3%, Sahifat al-Rida 99.5%. Sample: 980 chains read against the Arabic by the round-2 and round-3 re-checks (the round-3 random 320, its changed populations, and round-2 items unchanged since). Where: `datasets/hadith-data/chain-audit/structure-gate/README.md`.

**Known failure modes.** A name lost where the text names no one with a link word («أن X حدثه» alone); A Companion’s source named only in the matn («سمعتني أم الفضل»); Correct chains in many-route reports and the 15 small Imami works are left unchecked with the wrong ones.

**Reader sees.** “The reading of this chain’s routes has not been checked; it is not used for teacher and student lists”

**Excluded.** Three measured tests that removed no further defect: names out of order, a break inside one chain, length 12 or more.

**Credited.** `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/pg_export/chain_structure.py`.

### Isnad identity reviewer {#specialist-isnad-identity}

`isnad-identity` version `1.0.0` · AI specialist review · Ready for its pilot

**Question.** Is this name, at this position of this chain, this person?

**System prompt.** [`reviews/ai/prompts/isnad-identity.md`](../../reviews/ai/prompts/isnad-identity.md) (version and SHA-256 in `reviews/ai/specialists.json`).

**Packet.** The Arabic text and the chain as written; The target position with its neighbours; Candidates in a neutral order, each with who asserts it; Rijal passages with locators where linked; Glossary definitions. Nothing about how the pipeline scored the claim.

**Recommended model.** `claude-opus-5-5`: Rijal reasoning over classical Arabic; Fable 5.2 only for contested names and the Imams’ kunyas. Not: Any model that produced the candidate (Riwayat’s automatic linking used Claude labels: review those with a non-Claude model or flag the overlap).

**Measured agreement.** None yet. Pilot not yet run.

## Tellings of the same report {#correspondence}

Reports are linked, never narrators or chains. A link is evidence that two texts correspond, not a ruling that they are one hadith.

### Shared wording between two report texts {#correspondence-textual-overlap}

`correspondence-textual-overlap` version `report-correspondence-v1` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** With the chains set aside, two texts share enough five-letter sequences to be shown as tellings of one report: same wording at 80 % shared, variant wording at 40 % or more, or a passage covering 70 % or more of the shorter text. Texts under eight words are not compared.

**Evidence.** Both report texts, each bound by its SHA-256; The matn of each, isolated from its chain.

**Measured.** Pairs read as plainly the same report: same wording 24 of 24; variant wording at 40 % or more 45 of 48; shared passage at 70 % or more 35 of 40. Recall against exact scoring: 77 % overall, 100 % for same wording. Sample: 150 pairs read by the job’s author (one reader, not a reviewer); recall on 450 reports scored exactly. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/report-correspondence/README.md §Precision, §Recall`.

**Known failure modes.** A shared formula carries the overlap: the shahada, the tahlil, a Qur’an verse, the frame ثلاثة لا يكلمهم الله with different triads; The same ruling attributed to different speakers; Short sayings are missed (under eight words).

**Reader sees.** “AI-reviewed (checked by rule): shared wording”

**Credited.** `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/report-correspondence/correspondence_logic.py`, `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/report-correspondence/matn_isolation.py`.

### Shared wording after removing formulas (second version) {#correspondence-textual-overlap-v2}

`correspondence-textual-overlap-v2` version `report-correspondence-v2` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** As the first version, after cutting compiler remarks and setting aside formula spans and Qur’an quotations; short sayings match only when nearly identical, and a short saying quoted inside a longer report is its own class.

**Evidence.** Both report texts; A formula inventory built from the whole corpus; The Qur’an text (Tanzil).

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. In progress; no precision reading yet.

**Known failure modes.** Not yet known.

**Reader sees.** “AI-reviewed (checked by rule): shared wording”

**Credited.** `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/report-correspondence-v2/correspondence_logic_v2.py`.

### Report correspondence reviewer {#specialist-correspondence}

`correspondence` version `1.0.0` · AI specialist review · Ready for its pilot

**Question.** Are these two texts tellings of the same report, a shared passage, a shared formula or verse, the same ruling from another speaker, or unrelated?

**System prompt.** [`reviews/ai/prompts/correspondence.md`](../../reviews/ai/prompts/correspondence.md) (version and SHA-256 in `reviews/ai/specialists.json`).

**Packet.** Both texts in full, labelled A and B in a neutral order; Their locators, for citing only; Glossary definitions. Nothing about how the pipeline scored the claim.

**Recommended model.** `claude-opus-5-5`: Close reading of classical Arabic wording; volume is handled by sampling, not a weaker model.

**Measured agreement.** None yet. Pilot not yet run.

## English translations {#translation}

English supplied by a source is credited to its translator. English made here is a machine translation, labelled with the model.

### Machine translation with a quality screen {#translation-machine-qa-screen}

`translation-machine-qa-screen` version `screen-v2` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** The pinned model translates the Arabic only; the output is kept only if it passes the screen: not blank, not a refusal or placeholder, no Arabic letters left, at least 80 % Latin letters, a plausible length against the Arabic, no repetition loop, and a normal finish.

**Evidence.** The Arabic text, bound by its SHA-256; The model’s output and the provider’s run record.

**Measured.** 7 of 58 outputs read against their Arabic had a meaning-level error (12 %, about one in eight), in line with the first pilot’s one in seven; four of the seven read a common noun as a proper name. Sample: 58 outputs drawn at random by work and length, one reader (the lane’s agent); not a reviewed measurement. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/translation-run-2/README.md §Reading of 58 outputs`.

**Known failure modes.** A changed meaning in fluent English (a gift rendered as an oath); A speaker dropped or added; Name spellings drift between rows.

**Reader sees.** “Unreviewed machine translation (model named); the screen checks form, not meaning”

**Excluded.** Source-provided English is the source’s own and is credited to its translator; it is not AI-reviewed.

**Credited.** `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/generate_hy_mt2_candidates.py`, `datasets/hadith-data/translation_model.json`.

### Translation reviewer {#specialist-translation}

`translation` version `1.0.0` · AI specialist review · Prompt written, not yet run

**Question.** Does the English say what the Arabic says? List every meaning error.

**System prompt.** [`reviews/ai/prompts/translation.md`](../../reviews/ai/prompts/translation.md) (version and SHA-256 in `reviews/ai/specialists.json`).

**Packet.** The Arabic text; The English to review; The transliteration note and glossary terms. Nothing about how the pipeline scored the claim.

**Recommended model.** `claude-opus-5-5`: Independent of the translators; strong on classical Arabic. Not: tencent/hy-mt2-30b-a3b (the pinned translator); google/gemini-2.5-flash for its own candidates.

**Measured agreement.** None yet. Not yet run.

## Gradings and verdicts {#grading}

A grade is always one scholar’s ruling within one tradition. The archive computes no grade.

### Grading attributed to a named scholar {#grading-attribution}

`grading-attribution` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** A grade is shown only as one scholar’s ruling within one tradition, in the scholar’s words, with the work, volume and page the source records. Entries that are not rulings (“he did not include it”, “he was silent on it”, back-references) are excluded. No grade is computed, mapped to another scale or combined.

**Evidence.** The grading entry as the source records it; The grader’s name and the cited work and locator.

**Measured.** Every one of 16,835 Imami grading entries parsed into grader, term and locator (0 failures); 1,813 non-rulings excluded. Sample: All entries, by code. The attribution itself has not been checked against the cited works. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/grading/README.md; datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/grading-recovery/README.md`.

**Known failure modes.** A ruling about a different chain of the same report; Spelling variants of one term counted as different terms.

**Reader sees.** “Attributed ruling (as the source records it); AI-reviewed means the attribution was parsed, not that the ruling was checked in the work”

**Credited.** `THQ` Thaqalayn (Stichting Thaqalayn).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/grading-recovery/build_hadith_assessment_rows.py`.

### A compiler’s own statement in the text {#grading-compiler-statement}

`grading-compiler-statement` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** A grade term that follows the compiler’s own speaker phrase (قال أبو عيسى in al-Tirmidhi) is quoted with its exact character span in the Arabic. Statements where another authority is quoted, or no grade term appears, are held back.

**Evidence.** The Arabic text with the statement’s character span.

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. Not measured; 2,707 statements found and 785 held back, every one awaiting review.

**Known failure modes.** A quoted authority mistaken for the compiler.

**Reader sees.** “Compiler’s statement (quoted from the text)”

**Credited.** `SUN` sunnah.com (via Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-dataset”).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/extract_tirmidhi_compiler_statements.py`.

### A collection’s criterion, not a grade {#grading-compiler-criterion}

`grading-compiler-criterion` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** A report in a collection whose compiler set a standard for the whole work is linked to that standard, never given a grade of its own.

**Evidence.** The work the report belongs to.

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. Nothing to measure: membership in the work decides it. The criterion text itself still needs a citation.

**Known failure modes.** None in the link; the criterion’s wording needs a cited source.

**Reader sees.** “The collection’s criterion (not a grade of this report)”

**Credited.** `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/grading-recovery/build_hadith_assessment_rows.py`.

### Collection-wide labels are never grades {#grading-collection-label-excluded}

`grading-collection-label-excluded` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** A label an upstream dataset put on every row of a collection (ثابت on all 29,915 rows of four works) is kept for the record and never shown as a grade.

**Evidence.** The label’s distribution across the dataset.

**Measured.** The label has one value on all 100,217 upstream rows, including both Sahihs, so it carries no per-report information. Sample: All rows, by code. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/grading/README.md (J6c)`.

**Reader sees.** “Not shown as a grade”

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/audit_pure_canon_ruling_label.py`.

### Grading attribution reviewer {#specialist-grading-attribution}

`grading-attribution` version `1.0.0` · AI specialist review · Prompt written, not yet run

**Question.** Does the passage state this ruling, by this scholar, about this report or narrator?

## Narrator dates, places and rijal entries {#biography}

Each rijal author’s entry is kept under that author and work; a narrator may have many.

### Narrator lexicon values, compared with Taqrib {#biography-lexicon-not-yet-cited}

`biography-lexicon-not-yet-cited` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In use

**Rule.** Dates, places and generations from the narrator lexicon are shown labelled “narrator lexicon, not yet cited”. Where the lexicon row links to an entry of Ibn Hajar’s Taqrib al-Tahdhib, the two are compared; the 61 values that conflict are held back until reviewed.

**Evidence.** The lexicon row; The linked Taqrib entry’s verbatim passage, entry number and page.

**Measured.** Death years agree or are consistent with Taqrib for 1,588 of 1,663 linked narrators that both date (95.5 %); generation 5,128 of 5,194 (98.7 %); places 3,195 agree, 20 differ. The lexicon was very likely compiled from Taqrib-family works, so agreement mostly confirms faithful copying. Sample: All 5,404 Taqrib-linked lexicon rows, by code. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/biography-verification/README.md`.

**Known failure modes.** Digit slips in the lexicon; Typos in the digital Taqrib (ست عسرة for ست عشرة); Century omitted by Ibn Hajar and read by his rule.

**Reader sees.** “Narrator lexicon, not yet cited”

**Credited.** `MSD` Muslim Scholars Database, Arees Institute (via Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-narrators”); `RIJ` OpenITI rijal texts.

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/biography-verification/verify_lexicon_against_rijal.py`.

### A value cited to a rijal passage {#biography-cited-rijal-passage}

`biography-cited-rijal-passage` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** A biographical value is cited when it is read from a verbatim passage of a named rijal work, with the author, edition, entry number and page, and attributed to that author within that author’s tradition. Several authors’ values are kept side by side, never merged.

**Evidence.** The verbatim passage with entry and page; The edition as its file header names it.

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. A 100-row spot-check worksheet is drawn but not yet read.

**Known failure modes.** A link to the wrong entry where two men share a name.

**Reader sees.** “Cited: <author>, <work>, entry <n>, vol. <v> p. <p>”

**Credited.** `RIJ` OpenITI rijal texts.

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/diagnostics/biography-verification/rijal_parsing.py`, `datasets/hadith-data/rijal/rijal_extract.py`.

### Rijal link reviewer {#specialist-rijal-link}

`rijal-link` version `1.0.0` · AI specialist review · Prompt written, not yet run

**Question.** Is this rijal entry about this narrator?

**System prompt.** [`reviews/ai/prompts/rijal-link.md`](../../reviews/ai/prompts/rijal-link.md) (version and SHA-256 in `reviews/ai/specialists.json`).

**Packet.** The narrator’s recorded names, teachers and students; The rijal entry verbatim with its locator; Other entries with the same headword. Nothing about how the pipeline scored the claim.

**Recommended model.** `claude-opus-5-5`: Homonym resolution in rijal works.

**Measured agreement.** None yet. Not yet run.

## Events and eras {#history}

Nothing historical is published without a cited passage.

### An event or era date stated by a cited passage {#history-cited-passage}

`history-cited-passage` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** A date is shown as AI-reviewed only when its citation is complete (book, author, printed edition, volume and page or entry, the exact Arabic passage, its position in the digital file and the file’s SHA-256) and the passage itself states the year, or the year heading it sits under in an annal does. An age, a duration, a reckoning such as the Year of the Elephant, or a missing century keeps the citation but not the label. When books differ, each date is its own cited claim; none is chosen. No language model is used.

**Evidence.** The cited passage from a chronicle or rijal work (Khalifa b. Khayyat, al-Tabari and others, from OpenITI) with its locator and file hash.

**Measured.** 182 date claims, all cited: 163 pass, 19 fail (15 century not written, 4 not stated as a year). 171 citations re-read from their spans with 0 failures. Of the 54 seeded events, 29 are supported by a cited passage, 2 are contradicted by it. Sample: Every claim, by code. Not yet read by a person. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/history/README.md §Results`.

**Known failure modes.** A date stated for a different event in the same year; A narrator’s presence reported only as “it is said”.

**Reader sees.** “AI-reviewed (checked by rule), source cited”

**Credited.** `OITI` OpenITI: a Machine-Readable Corpus of Islamicate Texts; `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive).

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/history/history_text.py`, `datasets/hadith-data/history/validate_citations.py`.

### History claim reviewer {#specialist-history-claim}

`history-claim` version `1.0.0` · AI specialist review · Prompt written, not yet run

**Question.** Does the cited passage state this date, place or event?

**System prompt.** [`reviews/ai/prompts/history-claim.md`](../../reviews/ai/prompts/history-claim.md) (version and SHA-256 in `reviews/ai/specialists.json`).

**Packet.** The claim; The cited passages with locators; The Hijri calendar note. Nothing about how the pipeline scored the claim.

**Recommended model.** `claude-fable-5-2`: Few items (92) and chronicle Arabic is hard; the strongest model costs little here.

**Measured agreement.** None yet. Not yet run.

## Qur’an citations {#quran}

Verse text and numbering come from the Tanzil Qur’an text.

### Qur’an quotation found by exact letter match {#quran-citation-letter-match}

`quran-citation-letter-match` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** A span of the report is a Qur’an quotation when its letters, after folding spelling differences between the Uthmani and plain scripts, match a verse exactly; the span is recorded by character offsets in the stored text and bound by its hash. Short common phrases and formulas are kept apart from citations.

**Evidence.** The report text; The Tanzil Qur’an text, Simple Clean and Uthmani.

**Measured.** Spans classed as citations were real quotations in 51 of 54 read (94 %). Of hadith-kg’s own quotations that can be located, 1,206 of 1,262 (95.6 %) are found whole. Sample: 80 matches read by one reader (not a scholar); recall measured by code against hadith-kg on Sunni reports. Where: `datasets/hadith-data/quran/README.md §Reading of 80 matches, §Validation`.

**Known failure modes.** A common phrase that also occurs in the Qur’an; Short cued quotations of four words.

**Reader sees.** “Qur’an citation (checked by rule)”

**Credited.** `SWI` Shura wa Istehsan (this archive); `HKG` hadith-kg (“al-Jami — Hadith Knowledge Graph”) by emadjumaah.

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/quran/quran_logic.py`.

## Report numbers and editions {#numbering}

Each provider is referred to in its own scheme.

### Report numbers in each source’s own scheme {#numbering-source-scheme}

`numbering-source-scheme` version `2026.11.21` · Checked by rule · In progress

**Rule.** Each report is referred to in its provider’s own numbering; a number cell that is a marker, a grade word or empty is not read as a number, and every irregularity is flagged rather than repaired.

**Evidence.** The provider’s number cell and URL.

**Measured.** No measured accuracy. Not measured.

**Known failure modes.** Numbering that restarts per chapter (al-Kafi).

**Reader sees.** “Number as the source gives it”

**Credited.** `SUN` sunnah.com (via Kaggle “fahd09/hadith-dataset”); `THQ` Thaqalayn (Stichting Thaqalayn); `OITI` OpenITI: a Machine-Readable Corpus of Islamicate Texts; `NMC` NabiMuhammad.com, Hadith Pure Canon Authentica.

**Code.** `datasets/hadith-data/reconciled/structure/structure_logic.py`, `src/lib/citation/reference.ts`.
